subject: Response entropy: hosted API 5xx spike and rollback timeline
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma@greencrest.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Nov 2028 08:03:00 +0000
Subject: Response entropy: hosted API 5xx spike and rollback timeline

Hi Emma —

We saw a short but widespread increase in 5xx and timeout responses hitting hosted inference between 07:45–09:30 UTC this morning that impacted a subset of GreenCrest traffic. I wanted to send a concise customer advisory and what we've done so far. Summary below, TL;DR at the top.

TL;DR
- Impact: ~12% of API calls for GreenCrest experienced 502/504 or truncated responses between 07:45–08:50 UTC, with retry amplification observed on client SDKs.
- Current status: Mitigated — automatic routing policies rolled back to model-variant rwd-stable-1 (08:50 UTC). Traffic normalized; we continue to monitor.

What happened (short):
- A control-plane routing change allowed a small number of requests to be routed into a pool that briefly experienced fanout amplification at the edge proxies. That amplified backend load and led to transient proxy backpressure; downstream inference nodes returned 502/504 while the control plane retried, producing the 5xx spike we observed. We’re calling this a "response entropy" event — amplified request fanout causing short-lived failure waves.

Immediate actions we took:
1) Identified failing routing variant and shifted traffic back to the stable model variant (08:50 UTC).
2) Enabled temporary rate-limiting at the edge for higher-concurrency keys to stop retry amplification (08:55 UTC).
3) Scoped affected customer keys and prioritized remediation for GreenCrest so your requests hit the stable routing path (09:05 UTC).

Impact to GreenCrest:
- We see a ~12% error rate during the window above. We preserved request ordering and most requests completed after automatic fallback; however, a minority saw truncation and required client-side retry.

Attachments: ops-playbook.pdf (post-incident steps), response-entropy-summary.csv (per-key error breakdown).

Ask:
- Can you confirm by EOD if you observed downstream duplicate/partial side-effects we should flag for your engineers?
- We'll send a follow-up postmortem and a short remediation checklist with SDK recommendations (retry backoff adjustments).

I’ll follow up with Ben and Marissa on technical root cause details. We’ve flagged this incident on our status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incident/2028-11-16-response-entropy

Thanks and sorry for the disruption —

2) Any guidance on recommended backoff windows — our client retries at 250ms x 3 and that appears to have made things worse during the spike.

Appreciate the rollback and will watch the status link.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Emma Chen <emma@greencrest.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Nov 2028 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Response entropy: hosted API 5xx spike and rollback timeline

Folks — quick technical summary and next steps (internal + shared with customer):

Root cause (initial triage):
- A lightweight control-plane optimization that expanded fanout for ultra-low-latency variants incorrectly included a subset of tenant routing keys. Under a brief surge the edge proxies produced a small amplification loop (retries from the control plane + client SDK retries). The proxies hit transient connection limits and returned 502/504.
- Secondary factor: aggressive client retry windows (<=250ms) amplified the transient failures into more visible customer impact.

Data points:
- Spike window: 07:46–08:49 UTC. Peak 5xx rate at 07:58 UTC.
- Affected instances: edge-proxy cluster ep-usw-12 (high CPU; ephemeral socket exhaustion) and model-serving pool rwd-enc-7.
- Safeguards triggered: automated routing rollback at 08:50 UTC; ephemeral circuit-breakers closed affected proxy endpoints at 08:52 UTC.

Immediate remediation completed:
- Rollback to rwd-stable-1 (08:50 UTC).
- Edge rate-limits and an adaptive retry-suppressor enabled for high-concurrency tenant keys (08:55 UTC).
- Removed the control-plane expansion patch from staged rollout (09:15 UTC).

Next steps (24–72h):
- Root cause postmortem with timeline and code-level fix for control-plane optimizer (owner: infra-routing team).
- Permanent guardrails: per-tenant fanout limits and a soft-throttle at the edge to prevent retry amplification (owner: edge infra).
- Customer guidance: SDK backoff update to exponential jitter starting at 500ms for 5xxs; we'll publish a short note in the SDK repo.

I'll put the initial incident log and the CSV extract into the shared incident folder and attach the summary here. CC'ing Hannah to run the postmortem doc template and schedule a 1-hour follow-up with GreenCrest if they want one.

-ben

Subject: Re: Response entropy: hosted API 5xx spike and rollback timeline — short summary and next steps

Emma —

Thanks for the quick confirmation earlier. Per your asks: attached is response-entropy-summary.csv (per-key breakdown) and the ops-playbook.pdf that includes SDK backoff guidance. Quick summary and actions for GreenCrest: 

1) Impact window: 07:46–08:49 UTC — ~12% error rate for affected keys.
2) We marked these keys for prioritized routing to the stable pool; your ingestion pipeline should see reduced duplicates after dedupe pass.
3) Recommended client change: increase initial retry to 500ms with exponential backoff + random jitter; we will push a short snippet to the SDK repo today.
4) Follow-up: we'll run a joint 30–45 minute postmortem with your team early next week (options: Mon/Tue) to walk timeline, tracer logs, and remediation. Please tell us which slot you prefer.

Internal owners/contacts: Ben Carter (technical lead — ben_carter@redwood.com), Marissa Cole (customer lead — marissa_cole@redwood.com), Hannah Schmitt (postmortem facilitator — hannah_schmitt@redwood.com).

We'll update the status page with the final postmortem link once the doc is published. Thanks for your partnership while we worked the rollback.

Best,
